title: From Partners to Populations: A Hierarchical Bayesian Account of Coordination and Convention
one_sentence: CHAI 已形式化 partner-specific common ground 如何在多个时间尺度上与 community conventions 共存并发生 transfer。
problem: Dyad-specific flexibility 如何与 population-wide stable conventions 共存，且局部互动经验如何向陌生伙伴泛化？
method: 提出 Continual Hierarchical Adaptation through Inference (CHAI)，结合 repeated natural-language communication experiments 与 hierarchical Bayesian simulations。
findings: 模型与实验覆盖同伴内 referring efficiency、partner-specific knowledge 向 strangers 的渐进 transfer，以及 communicative context 对最终 convention 的影响。
real_contribution: 为 dyad→population convention transfer 提供理论与计算 baseline，阻止 AMSC 把 generic lifecycle/transfer theory 当成空白。
biggest_weakness: 计算可扩展性、online incrementality 与现实开放环境仍有限；没有 embodied multimodal Agent。
claim_boundary: 解决 generic human convention transfer 的理论缺口，不解决 embodied human–AI 中如何在线检测、协商、修复或迁移 mapping。
why_researcher_should_care: 要求下一步 novelty 建立在现有 multi-timescale convention theory 之上，而非把 partner-specific 与 transferable convention 错误对立。

amsc.master_list_decision: Candidate — Must Read / Recovered theory anchor

evidence_notes: Recovered classic outside the strict seven-day window; journal DOI and open manuscript were verified.
Included because it materially narrows the program's transfer/lifecycle novelty claim.
